note: oam@1: for each of the 1 197 CBSE (NCERT) and Tamil Nadu State Board outcomes (content/learning/syllabus), which question families, written tasks and authored questions really assess it, and whether every part of the statement is assessed at its level (full), only part (partial, with what is missing) or nothing (none). Judged from the content itself — sampled problems of every family of the mapped competencies — by AI assessors working to a written brief, after an independent audit found that mapping alone overclaimed. Provisional: not educator-reviewed. The coverage compiler calls an outcome engineering-complete only where this map says full and fit. oam@2: the outcomes first judged partial or none were judged again, afresh, by new assessors after the gap@1 content was added (new families, everyday forms, written tasks and remaps).

outcomes.missing: Shapes are never shown in different sizes, and squares are never shown tilted (e.g. as a diamond); orientation is limited to triangle glyphs pointing four ways and rectangles standing or lying, pitched at Grade 1.
Checking the sum by estimating: no estimation family is mapped to this outcome (adestchk sits under estimate-check, which is mapped only to the subtraction outcome).
Census-style word problems: every mapped family is a bare sum (acstory4, which has four-digit stories, is not mapped here).
Finding increases and decreases in context: the mapped families are bare four-digit subtractions.
Mirror images of digits, and describing what a mirror image looks like (aemirror only asks which whole word looks unchanged; aedigsym asks lines of symmetry, not mirror images).

Estimating large quantities (thousands and more) such as travel distances: the mapped estimation families round two- and three-digit numbers and prices (abunit and aernd, which do this, are not mapped here).
Recognising that the same fraction looks different in different wholes; grids are only shaded or named, never compared across wholes of different sizes.
Complements to 1000: admental covers 100 and 10,000 and leaves 1000 to ad1000, which is in a competency not mapped to this outcome.

Mental-calculation strategies are not assessed by the mapped content (e.g. compensation or regrouping to round numbers to get an exact result); only rounding-based estimation and judging whether a result is reasonable or about how big it is.
Word problems are not assessed: fadd, faddu and avfas are all bare calculations (no story or measurement context).

Converting from the international system back to the Indian system (millions to lakhs/crores) and billions are not assessed: ajmill only turns crores into millions, and ajcrore's pool has no million/billion items despite its stated limits.
Judging the size of large quantities (e.g. how many days 1 lakh seconds is, or whether 1 crore of something is plausible) is not asked; only products with powers of ten and estimates of products are.
Money word problems are not assessed: agrupee gives only bare rupee sums and differences (measurement problems are covered by agmeas).

Exploring patterns in the Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers (e.g. sums of terms, which terms are even) is not asked: ahfib has a single form asking for a later term, and ahrhy covers only the counting link.

Real-life problems that apply the theorem itself to find a length (ladder, pole, diagonal of a field) are not asked: ahpyth is bare triangles; real-life contexts appear only in ahconv (a mason checking a right angle with the converse).
Building a display with a spreadsheet is not assessed: wr:disp:infographic-story only asks the learner to name one thing a spreadsheet would make easier (this part cannot be done in the app).
The algebra-tile stage (factorising by arranging tiles into a rectangle) is not assessed and cannot be done in the app; splitting the middle term is.

Perimeters of polygons are asked only for rectangles at Grade 4 level (rperim, avfence) plus the hexagon in the written task; perimeters of other polygons (triangles, irregular or regular polygons) are not asked.
Describing randomness (what makes an experiment random, unpredictable single outcomes) is not asked; placing events on the 0-1 scale in words and numbers is.
Relating an AP to everyday contexts is not asked: no item in apn, auapis, auapk, auaps, auapc, auaprec or auapln has a real-life setting (checked all items).

Listing the divisors of a number efficiently by pairing divisors up to its square root is asked only for numbers up to 100 (agfac, Grade 5 level); the square-root bound itself is asked only for primality testing (agptest).
Relating the HCF algorithms to Aryabhata's division method is not asked (Aryabhata appears only in teaching text).

Forming a quadratic equation from a situation is never itself asked: auqwp says 'form a quadratic equation' but check only the final root, which can be found by trial; auqstd covers recognising and standard form only.
Everyday problems (savings, instalments, arrangements) are not assessed: apn, auaps and auapk ask only for terms and sums of bare APs, with no context in any of their 3,360 problems.
combinations with a cuboid or a whole sphere are not asked (cube combinations are)
combinations with a cuboid or a whole sphere are not asked (cube combinations are)
Range of real functions other than quadratics on ℝ (e.g. rational, square-root or modulus functions); aorange is quadratics only.
Writing the combined function (f + g)(x), (f − g)(x), (fg)(x), (f/g)(x) as an expression; alfop only evaluates the combination at a point, and the domain is asked only for f/g of linear functions.
Sketching the graphs of sin x, cot x and cosec x; the written tasks sketch only cos (y = 3 cos 2x), tan and sec.
Temperature and mixture word problems: every aeineqw item is a test-marks average or a trip budget (its limits mention temperatures, but no item in the pool has one).
Comparison of numbers by the binomial expansion (e.g. which is larger, (1.01)^1000000 or 10000); aobinapp only evaluates exactly or approximates.

Estimating a limit from a table of values or from a graph: every aultab item (despite its title) computes a one-sided limit of a piecewise-linear formula; nothing asks whether the limit exists by comparing the two one-sided limits.
Sums and differences that include trigonometric terms (e.g. x³ + 2 sin x − cos x); audsum is polynomials only, and quotients with trigonometric functions are only sin x/(x + a).
Mean deviation about the median for continuous (class-interval) frequency data; atmdf's grouped items are about the mean only.
Graphs of cot⁻¹, sec⁻¹ and cosec⁻¹; the written tasks sketch only cos⁻¹, sin⁻¹ and tan⁻¹.
Word problems with lengths in mixed units; aemix, aemulm and aedivm give bare calculations.

Ordering numbers or items by a stated rule other than size (for example by a property or a given criterion); only ascending/descending order of numbers is asked, and the enumeration families list arrangements rather than order them.
Expanded form of numbers in crores and millions is not assessed: aenumf's expanded forms stop at six digits (lakhs); reading, writing and comma placement in both systems are covered.

Estimating sums, differences and products of large numbers in real-life settings is not asked: the estimation items use bare two- to four-digit numbers, and the only real-life estimate (adestcost) totals small prices.
Listing the arrangements or combinations that meet given conditions in an organised way is not asked: aksarr only counts them, and the only listing task (wr:enum-outfits, Grade 4) has no conditions.
Money word problems are not assessed: agrupee gives only bare rupee sums and differences (measurement problems are covered by agmeas).
Word problems with rational numbers are not asked: every ajrq and ajinv item is a bare operation (checked all items).
The long-division method for square roots is not assessed: ahsqd and aksqf check only the final root, which can be found by trial squaring.

Perimeters of combined shapes are asked only for rectangle-plus-semicircle gardens (6 of 450 amcshape items) and rectangular L-shapes; perimeters of combined shapes with triangles, trapeziums or sectors are not asked (their areas are).
Applying the compound-interest formula to growth (population, bacteria and the like) is not asked; ajci has only interest and depreciation (checked all items).
The link between repeated-division HCF and Fibonacci numbers is not asked: aeeuc uses neighbouring Fibonacci pairs but never points out or asks about the link.

Converting a terminating decimal to a fraction is not asked in the mapped families (amrec is recurring decimals only); fraction-to-decimal, recurring-to-fraction and deciding rational or irrational from the expansion are asked.
Converting from index form back to radical form is not asked: avfexp evaluates fractional powers and converts radicals to index form only.
Using (a+b+c)², products of three binomials and cubes of binomials to evaluate (e.g. 103³, or a²+b²+c² from a+b+c and ab+bc+ca) or to factorise is not asked; ahcube only expands.
Synthetic division as a method is not assessed (alcub checks only the zeros), and only monic cubics are factorised; non-monic cubics are not asked.
Long division versus synthetic division as methods is not assessed; only the quotient and remainder (division-algorithm form) are checked.

Deciding from an arrow diagram is not assessed (aoisfn uses ordered pairs, tables, point plots with the vertical line test and rules; none of its 190 problems is an arrow diagram), and representing a function in these forms is asked only once, as an arrow diagram in wr:fn:one-one-onto (a).
Recognising a real-valued function is never asked (one-one/many-one, onto/into, bijective, constant and identity are all in aofname/aqonto).
Word problems on arithmetic series are not assessed: auaps asks the sum of bare APs only, and wr:ap:derive-sum (c) is a bare number sum.
Solving by elimination is not seen: al3sys is answer-only and no written task asks for the elimination steps for three variables (almeth covers two variables only).
Range of functions other than quadratics on ℝ (e.g. rational, square-root or modulus functions); aorange is quadratics only.

Sketching the signum and step (greatest-integer) graphs: the task that asks for them (wr:std:sketch-recip-sgn-step) belongs to MATH.algebra.standard-function-graphs, which is not mapped to this outcome; the mapped content sketches only modulus, linear, quadratic, cubic and reciprocal graphs.
Solving a triangle completely (all remaining sides and angles); atsiner and atcosr each find one element, and atapp's limits leave full solution to written work, but no written task asks for it.
Arithmetic progressions in context: every AP family (apn, auapk, auaps, …) is a bare sequence; only the GP families (aogpgr, aogpuse) have real situations.
Unit vectors and direction ratios: no item asks for a unit vector (â = a/|a|) or for direction ratios; atdc gives direction cosines only.

Estimating limits from tables and graphs, and deciding from the two one-sided limits whether the limit exists: aultab (despite its title) only computes one one-sided limit of a piecewise-linear formula.
Identifying infinite limits (e.g. 1/(x − a)² as x → a); auliinf has finite limits at infinity only and its limits exclude infinite limits.

Euler form re^(iθ), converting from polar back to rectangular form, and the modulus of a product or quotient in polar form; asarg gives only the principal argument and aspolm only the argument of z₁z₂ or z₁/z₂.
Sketching the graphs of cot⁻¹, sec⁻¹ and cosec⁻¹; the written tasks sketch only cos⁻¹, sin⁻¹ and tan⁻¹.
Writing the parametric equations of a conic: astaneh always states the parametrisation (e.g. x = 2 cos θ, y = sin θ) in the prompt, so no item asks the learner to write it.
The exponential indeterminate forms 0⁰ and ∞⁰ (e.g. lim x→0⁺ of xˣ); only the 1^∞ form appears (arlhop), and arlhinf's limits leave the others out.
Approximating a definite integral by a finite Riemann (left/right/mid-point) sum, and limits of sums over a general interval [a, b]; aurie only evaluates limits of sums over [0, 1].

Verifying that a general solution (with arbitrary constants) satisfies a differential equation, and telling general from particular solutions: only one particular solution is verified (wr:de:bacteria-growth); the task that does this (wr:hd:verify-general) is in MATH.calculus.higher-derivatives, which is not mapped to this outcome.
The one-point distribution (asbern, despite its title, has only Bernoulli and two-point items) and recognising which distribution a situation follows (every item names the distribution).
